records.name: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
records.summary:
A scattered South Atlantic territory of three island groups that legislated equality island by island: the 2009 constitutional order imposed by the administering state bans discrimination on grounds including sexual orientation across all three, and equal age of consent sits at 16. Marriage equality arrived in staggered fashion — the first dependency's council approved the ordinance 5-0 in May 2016 and it commenced January 2017, the most remote island followed in August 2017, and the principal island itself completed the set on 20 December 2017 — with adoption law following the same year.

The earlier profile undersold all of this as 'decriminalised' and added an unsourced 'church-conservative' gloss; neither survives the evidence. What is documented is a fast, orderly rights rollout across very small councils, and a total absence of survey data on social attitudes — remoteness, not resistance, is the characterised condition.

sources.summary: Alchetron mirror of the territory's LGBT-rights page (updated 25 Apr 2026): same-sex sexual activity legal; discrimination protections in force since 2009; same-sex marriage legal on Ascension Island since 2017 — the marriage-law jurisdiction of the territory.

GayLawNet laws index for the territory (page accessed 23 Jun 2013, citing ILGA State-sponsored Homophobia): consensual same-sex relations became lawful in 2001 and the age of consent is equalised at 16 territory-wide; page frames the territory as an Overseas Country or Territory of the EU (Charter applicability).

Wikiwand (Wikipedia mirror): LGBTQ rights in Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha - discrimination banned territory-wide since 2009; same-sex marriage legal since 2017 (Ascension 1 Jan, Tristan da Cunha 4 Aug, Saint Helena 20 Dec); adoption since 2017; detailed vote records of the Ascension Island Council (5-0).

Wikiwand (Wikipedia mirror, redirects to the territory article): LGBTQ rights on Ascension Island - the marriage ordinance approved 31 May 2016 (5-0), signed and gazetted 20 June, commenced 1 January 2017.

records.name: Pitcairn Islands
records.summary:
Pitcairn's roughly fifty inhabitants govern family law themselves, and on paper they have adopted the most complete equality package in this group of territories: activity legal since 2001, a 2010 constitution that bans sexual-orientation discrimination, and a 2015 Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance — marriage defined as the union of two people regardless of sex, orientation or gender identity, foreign civil partnerships recognised, and adoption open to married, unmarried and single people alike.

The earlier profile's 'Christian-conservative, no public LGBT life' clause appeared in no source and has been deleted; it was the only stated basis for placing this territory below its administering state, which the legal record does not support. What the sources do say is that no islander is known to be in a same-sex relationship — on an island this size, invisibility is arithmetic rather than atmosphere, and defence is the administering state's responsibility.

sources.summary: Alchetron mirror of the Wikipedia article (updated 25 Apr 2026): Pitcairn Islands (British overseas territory) — same-sex activity legal since 2001; 2010 Constitution bans sexual-orientation discrimination (protections 'since 2010'); same-sex marriage legal since 14 May 2015 and adoption since 2015; none of c. 50 residents is known to be in a same-sex relationship; military service under UK responsibility.

Readable Wiki mirror (Wikipedia, CC BY-SA): discrimination on sexual orientation banned by the 2010 Pitcairn Constitution Order; marriage defined as union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity; same-sex marriage legal since 14 May 2015; the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 also recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn; adoption open to married, unmarried and single people.

Full Wikipedia republication: same-sex sexual activity legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001; anti-discrimination constitutional protection from the 2010 Constitution Order; same-sex marriage legal 14 May 2015 — ordinance unanimously approved by the Island Council 1 Apr 2015, signed by Governor Jonathan Sinclair 5 May, published 13 May 2015; adoption legal since 2015; page also indexes the territory within UK LGBT-rights timelines.

records.name: Guernsey
records.summary:
A self-governing Crown Dependency with its own parliament, Guernsey moved briskly through the 2010s: in 2011 it aligned blood-donation rules with the metropole, ending the HIV-era ban on gay and bisexual donors; in June 2015 the states rewrote the adoption law to open adoption to same-sex couples, removing a fifty-year bar on unmarried couples; and in December 2015 the states approved same-sex marriage 37-7, rejecting civil-partnership and secular-union alternatives as insufficient, with the law itself commencing from spring 2018.

That record covers sexual orientation squarely; the position on gender identity was asserted in the earlier profile without any cited source and has been deleted, so a transgender visitor should treat legal gender recognition and trans-specific protection as unestablished here — the more notable local quirk being that, on the documented chronology, civil partnership arrived later than in the neighbouring dependency that shares the island group's institutions.

sources.summary: Guernsey Billet d'État (24 June 2015): official States of Guernsey legislative business document - includes the review of Adoption Law (p.1170) that led to same-sex couples' adoption rights.

BBC (10 Dec 2015): States of Guernsey approved same-sex marriage 37-7, rejecting both civil-partnership-only and single 'Union Civile' alternatives; implementing legislation separate and not expected before 2017. Charity Liberate: 'historic day'; debate described as 'extremely positive'.

BBC (24 Jun 2015): Guernsey repealed its 50-year Adoption Law's ban on unmarried couples adopting — States agreed same-sex couples may adopt, with civil partnerships recognised and equal parental responsibility for both partners (Jersey had approved the same change two days earlier).

BBC (23 Sep 2011): Guernsey adopted the UK's relaxed blood-donor rules — gay/bisexual men eligible after 12-month deferral, targeted ~7 Nov 2011 to match the UK change, ending the local 1980s HIV-era ban; other donation restrictions unchanged.

records.name: Isle of Man
records.summary:
Isle of Man: a self-legislating Crown Dependency in the Irish Sea whose parliament, Tynwald, works through its own bills on these questions. The House of Keys in 2005 proactively adopted a clause protecting employees from dismissal over sexual orientation, framing it in human-rights terms; the chief minister publicly committed to marriage equality in 2015, at a time when this parliament and Northern Ireland's assembly were the only British legislatures refusing it; the Marriage and Civil Partnership (Amendment) Bill passed its final legislative stages in April 2016 and the first civil partnership was converted to marriage that July, preserving the couple's 2015 wedding date.

Current reference material confirms the settled picture: civil partnerships from 2011, marriage since 2016, and a legal gender-recognition right in force since 2009 alongside 'gender reassignment' protections in island equality law. Claims about the metropole's single-sex code and its statutory guidance were carried in the earlier profile without primary legislative support and have been deleted, leaving

sources.summary: Tynwald Hansard (26 April 2016): Legislative Council proceedings - Third Reading of the Marriage and Civil Partnership (Amendment) Bill 2016 (same-sex marriage) and consideration of the Equality Bill 2016 - the primary legislative record of the Isle of Man's marriage-equality debate.

BBC (28 Jul 2016): same-sex marriage took effect on the island after Royal Assent of the Marriage and Civil Partnership Act (2015-16 law reform); the first civil-partnership-to-marriage conversion was completed days after entry into force, with civil partnerships (legal since 2011) convertible without a second ceremony — confirming a smooth, routine registration process for couples.

BBC (30 Nov 2005): the House of Keys adopted an Employment Bill amendment protecting gay and lesbian employees from dismissal on sexual-orientation grounds (tabling by Onchan MHK Peter Karran) — the island's employment non-discrimination milestone, aligned with UK human-rights law.

3FM (9 Jun 2015): Chief Minister Allan Bell publicly backed same-sex marriage and said he would formulate a bill to repeal the island's marriage prohibition — the political commitment that preceded the 2016 Marriage and Civil Partnership Act.
